marrow__ANAT_CH57_Q015.takeaway: Morton's neuroma usually involves the third common plantar digital nerve, typically a branch of the medial plantar nerve.
marrow__ANAT_CH57_Q015.displayText:
Morton's neuroma usually involves the third common plantar digital nerve, typically a branch of the medial plantar nerve.

Morton's neuroma may occur due to entrapment of branches of the medial plantar nerve.

The source identifies entrapment of the third common digital nerve, a branch of the medial plantar nerve, as the common pattern.

The medial plantar nerve can also be compressed at the Knot of Henry, where the flexor hallucis longus tendon passes deep to the flexor digitorum longus tendon to reach the medial sole.
emphasis: Morton's neuroma usually involves the third common plantar digital nerve, typically a branch of the medial plantar nerve

rationales.a: The sural nerve supplies the lateral foot skin and does not form the common digital nerve in the forefoot web space.
rationales.c: The superficial fibular nerve supplies most dorsal foot skin, not the plantar digital nerve at the metatarsal heads.
rationales.d: The saphenous nerve supplies medial leg/foot border skin, not the interdigital plantar nerve affected in Morton's neuroma.

marrow__ANAT_CH57_Q016.takeaway: Baxter's nerve is the first branch of the lateral plantar nerve and can be compressed near the abductor hallucis fascia.
marrow__ANAT_CH57_Q016.displayText:
Baxter's nerve is the first branch of the lateral plantar nerve and can be compressed near the abductor hallucis fascia.

Baxter's nerve is a branch of the lateral plantar nerve.

Compression of Baxter's nerve by the deep fascia covering abductor hallucis is implicated as a possible cause of chronic heel pain and plantar fasciitis.
emphasis: Baxter's nerve is the first branch of the lateral plantar nerve and can be compressed near the abductor hallucis fascia

rationales.a: Medial calcaneal branches arise from the tibial nerve before its plantar division and are not Baxter's nerve.
rationales.b: Lateral calcaneal branches are cutaneous branches to the heel, not Baxter's motor/sensory branch.
rationales.c: Medial plantar nerve supplies medial sole muscles and digital branches; Baxter's nerve is from lateral plantar.

marrow__ANAT_CH57_Q017.takeaway: The cremasteric reflex has L1–L2 roots; the genitofemoral nerve carries its afferent and efferent limbs.
marrow__ANAT_CH57_Q017.displayText:
The cremasteric reflex has L1–L2 roots; the genitofemoral nerve carries its afferent and efferent limbs.

The cremasteric reflex is mediated by L1 and L2. Stroking the medial thigh produces ipsilateral elevation of the testicle.

Afferent limb: femoral branch of the genitofemoral nerve. Efferent limb: genital branch of the genitofemoral nerve.
emphasis: The cremasteric reflex has L1–L2 roots; the genitofemoral nerve carries its afferent and efferent limbs

rationales.b: L3–L4 are not the roots classically assigned to the cremasteric reflex.
rationales.c: S1–S2 mediate other sacral reflexes, not the cremasteric response.
rationales.d: T8–T9 are thoracic dermatomes and do not mediate cremasteric elevation.

marrow__ANAT_CH57_Q018.takeaway: The deep circumflex iliac artery branches from the external iliac artery; the superficial pudendal/circumflex branches arise from femoral artery.
marrow__ANAT_CH57_Q018.displayText:
The deep circumflex iliac artery branches from the external iliac artery; the superficial pudendal/circumflex branches arise from femoral artery.

The deep circumflex iliac artery is a branch of the external iliac artery, not the femoral artery.

The femoral artery is the continuation of the external iliac artery behind the inguinal ligament. It descends through the femoral triangle and adductor canal, passes through the adductor hiatus and continues as the popliteal artery.

Branches listed by the source include superficial epigastric, superficial circumflex iliac, superficial external pudendal, deep external pudendal, muscular branches, profunda femoris and descending genicular artery.
emphasis: The deep circumflex iliac artery branches from the external iliac artery; the superficial pudendal/circumflex branches arise from femoral artery

rationales.b: The superficial external pudendal artery is a superficial branch of the femoral artery.
rationales.c: The superficial circumflex iliac artery is a branch of the femoral artery.
rationales.d: Deep external pudendal branches arise from femoral artery and supply external genital skin.

marrow__ANAT_CH57_Q019.takeaway: The cruciate anastomosis includes transverse circumflex femoral branches, inferior gluteal and first perforating branches; superior gluteal is not a component.
marrow__ANAT_CH57_Q019.displayText:
The cruciate anastomosis includes transverse circumflex femoral branches, inferior gluteal and first perforating branches; superior gluteal is not a component.

The superior gluteal artery does not contribute to the cruciate anastomosis.

Cruciate anastomosis lies at the level of the lesser trochanter and is formed by transverse branches of the medial and lateral circumflex femoral arteries, the descending branch of the inferior gluteal artery, and the ascending branch of the first perforating artery.

The source notes the clinical importance of lower-limb arterial anastomoses in trauma and hemorrhage control.
emphasis: The cruciate anastomosis includes transverse circumflex femoral branches, inferior gluteal and first perforating branches; superior gluteal is not a component

rationales.a: The first perforating artery contributes an ascending branch to the cruciate anastomosis.
rationales.b: The inferior gluteal artery contributes a descending branch to the anastomosis.
rationales.d: The lateral circumflex femoral artery contributes a transverse branch to the cruciate anastomosis.

marrow__ANAT_CH57_Q020.takeaway: The short saphenous vein usually drains into the popliteal vein, so that is the first deep vein reached by an embolus.
marrow__ANAT_CH57_Q020.displayText:
The short saphenous vein usually drains into the popliteal vein, so that is the first deep vein reached by an embolus.

A thrombus in the short saphenous vein may dislodge and enter the popliteal vein first. It can then travel to the right heart and potentially cause pulmonary embolism.

The short saphenous vein continues from the lateral side of the dorsal venous arch, passes behind the lateral malleolus and drains into the popliteal vein in the popliteal fossa. The popliteal vein continues proximally as the femoral vein.
emphasis: The short saphenous vein usually drains into the popliteal vein, so that is the first deep vein reached by an embolus

rationales.b: The femoral vein is reached after the popliteal vein continues proximally through the adductor hiatus.
rationales.c: Posterior tibial veins are deep tributaries of the popliteal, not the usual direct continuation of the short saphenous vein.
rationales.d: The great saphenous vein is a separate superficial medial vein and is not the short saphenous outflow.

marrow__ANAT_CH57_Q021.takeaway: Dodd perforators connect superficial and deep veins in the distal thigh above the knee.
marrow__ANAT_CH57_Q021.displayText:
Dodd perforators connect superficial and deep veins in the distal thigh above the knee.

Above-knee perforators are known as Dodd veins.

Perforator veins connect the deep and superficial venous systems. The source names proximal thigh perforators as Hunter perforators, distal thigh/above-knee perforators as Dodd perforators, below-knee perforators as Boyd perforators, and calf perforators as Cockett perforators.
emphasis: Dodd perforators connect superficial and deep veins in the distal thigh above the knee

rationales.b: Hunter perforators are generally described in the proximal thigh, not the distal above-knee group asked here.
rationales.c: Cockett perforators are in the lower leg/calf, not above the knee.
rationales.d: Boyd perforators are described around the knee/below-knee region, not the distal-thigh group above the knee.
